transcriptText:
Two hands. In one, you lost a big pot. In the other, you won... but weren't sure of the call. There's time to review one. Which one: the loss... or the unsure one? Pick first.

Here's a better way to keep score. Tag each decision by how confident you felt. Sure. Sure. Not sure. Not whether you won: grey the results out. Every unsure one goes to your review queue.

Why not review the losses? That plus-ten call from before still loses seventy times in a hundred. Every one, a good decision. Study only your losses... you mostly study good calls. So losses are a bad filter.

Once you've reviewed a spot, don't cram it. Decide it fresh now... then check it again later. Spaced practice beats cramming: a review of hundreds of experiments shows it. And the Academy schedules those checks for you.

So, which hand? The unsure one. More hands won't fix a decision you never look at. Review the decisions you weren't sure of... and come back to them later.
